# triops

> A small PHP web server for inspecting what IoT hardware actually sends over
> HTTP. Unzip into a web directory and it runs: no framework, no Composer
> packages, no database server, no build system, no third-party service.
> PHP 8.0+.

## What it is

triops is the receiving end of a device's HTTP connection during firmware
bring-up. A board posts a payload; triops shows the exact bytes, the headers,
the query string, and the arrival time. It also provides deliberately dumb
endpoints for testing client behaviour — a slow response, an arbitrary status
code, an exact byte count — because that is how you find out what a
microcontroller's HTTP client does under stress.

It is a bench tool, not a production telemetry backend. It keeps the last N
payloads per channel in a ring buffer and drops the rest.

## Two surfaces, and the line between them matters

- `/` — plain text, no envelope, no JSON. `timestamp.php`, `sum.php`, `ip.php`,
  `echo.php`, `headers.php`, `delay.php`, `code.php`, `bytes.php`. The audience
  is a device with a 2 KB HTTP client and a serial console. **Output formats
  here are a stability promise; people script against them.**
- `/api/` — JSON, versioned, always enveloped as
  `{"ok":bool,"api":int,"data":…}` or `{"ok":false,"error":…,"code":…}`.
  `version.php`, `status.php`, `read.php`, `ingest.php`, `clear.php`.

`api/version.php` is unauthenticated so a client can feature-detect. The `api`
integer changes only on a breaking API change, so nothing has to parse semver.

## Hard constraints

These are not preferences. Code that violates them does not belong in triops.

1. **Nothing to install alongside it.** No composer, no framework, no redis, no
   daemons, no cron, no build step. It needs PHP and a directory it can write to.
   The one vendored asset is bitwrench, pinned and committed, because a lab
   network may have no internet.
2. **File-per-URL routing.** No front controller, no router, no mod_rewrite
   requirement. A directory is a namespace; `api/v2/` is how the API versions.
3. **Runs on a plain shared host.** If it needs a long-running process or an
   uncommon extension, it does not ship in `app/`.
4. **PHP 8.0 floor.** No 8.1+ syntax (no enums, no readonly, no `never`).
5. **A new endpoint is ~5 lines** on top of the bootstrap. If it stops being
   that, the framework has failed and should be fixed rather than worked around.

## Layout

```
app/            the deployable unit — the release zip is exactly this directory
  lib/          triops.php (bootstrap), store.php, auth.php, ui.php
  api/          JSON endpoints
  templates/    plain.php, api.php, page.php — copy one to add a page
  assets/       bitwrench.umd.min.js (vendored, pinned), triops.js, logos
  data/         gitignored; sqlite db, ndjson files, users.php
docs/           markdown
pages/          GitHub Pages site: landing + a JS-mocked demo
dev/            scratch; ships in nothing
```

## How a page is written

Every page opens with one line:

```php
<?php require __DIR__ . '/lib/triops.php';
```

That provides config, the store, auth, and the response helpers. Then:

- plain text → `t_text($body)`
- JSON → `t_ok($data)` / `t_err($msg, $code, $status)`
- HTML → `t_page_open($title)` … `t_page_close(true, $data)` … `t_page_end()`

Auth guards: `t_require_auth()` on HTML pages (redirects to login/setup),
`t_api_require_auth()` under `api/` (returns 401 JSON — never redirect an API
client to an HTML form).

`t_channel($raw)` strips everything but `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`. Any user-supplied value
that reaches the filesystem must go through it.

## Storage

`t_store()` returns a driver implementing `push/last/clear/channels/healthy`.

- **sqlite** (default when `SQLite3` is present) — WAL mode, `busy_timeout`,
  trimmed inside the same transaction as the insert. WAL is required, not
  optional: the viewer polls while devices post, and rollback-journal mode
  throws "database is locked" under exactly that pattern.
- **ndjson** (fallback, no extensions) — append-only, `flock` + one `fwrite` per
  record, never read-modify-write. Line 1 of every data file is `<?php exit; ?>`
  so contents do not leak if the directory is ever served. Compacts at 4× the
  cap, so it retains between N and 4N.

Trimming happens on write. There is deliberately no cron and no timer.

## UI

The interface is [bitwrench](https://github.com/deftio/bitwrench) 2.x, vendored
at `app/assets/bitwrench.umd.min.js`. PHP emits a thin skeleton and passes data
as JSON on `window.TRIOPS_DATA`; the page script builds the DOM from TACO objects
(`{t, a, c, o}`). `bw.loadStyles()` derives the whole palette including dark
mode, so **there is no hand-written CSS in triops** — do not add any.

`app/assets/triops.js` adds what bitwrench cannot know about: `jsonTaco()`
renders arbitrary JSON as a browsable tree, `payloadTaco()` wraps it with a raw
toggle (and hex-dumps bodies that are not valid UTF-8), and `sanitizeTaco()`
enforces `docs/taco-wire.schema.json` on device-supplied TACO — an allowlist of
elements and attributes, not a filter, so anything not named is dropped.

Login and setup are the exception: they emit real HTML forms and work with
JavaScript disabled, because being locked out of a debug tool by a script error
is unacceptable.

## Security model

Users are humans who log in. Devices are not users — they post to
`api/ingest.php`, optionally gated by a shared `ingest_key` compared with
`hash_equals`. There are no roles: logged-in versus not is the only distinction.

Users live in `data/users.php`, not in the store, so auth still works when the
database is corrupt and you can fix a lockout with a text editor. Passwords are
`password_hash()`. Every state-changing form carries a CSRF token. There are no
default credentials — first run forces account creation.

## Where to read next

- `docs/hacking.md` — add your own page, including a short bitwrench primer
- `docs/api.md` — API reference
- `docs/troubleshooting.md` — device posts but nothing appears, etc.
- `docs/install.md` — nginx, shared hosting, moving the data directory
- `AGENTS.md` — conventions for editing this repo
